story.head: Expect the Devils to fire from everywhere
paras: The Capitals won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-2 in Washington on Oct 17. The Devils have won three straight, while the Capitals (8-6-0) lost 6-5 to Dallas on Nov 3. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Caps fourth (tied for 21st in the NHL) and the Devils second (tied for seventh).

The Capitals’ record (.571) is about what their chances are worth. The Devils have played better than their record (.688) says: their chances are worth about .745, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Capitals get the league’s best looks (1st) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (27th). As for the Devils, they keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest), rarely throw hits (3rd lowest) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (30th). The Devils are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Capitals. On top of that, both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Jordan Kyrou (5 G / 9 A / 14 P in 14 GP) leads the Capitals in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Alex Tuch (10 G / 2 A / 12 P in 14 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for tenth in the NHL. The Devils’ scoring runs through Jack Hughes (8 G / 13 A / 21 P in 16 GP), who has nine points in his last five games. Jesper Bratt (3 G / 12 A / 15 P in 16 GP) isn’t far behind.
Logan Thompson (5-4-0 / .887 SV% in 10 GS) will likely start for Washington, and Connor Hellebuyck (4-0-0 / .891 SV% in 4 GS) for New Jersey.
At home, Sheldon Keefe likes to send Meier, Hischier and Evangelista out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Tuch, Strome and Kyrou.
